nodes.speaker: Rohan
nodes.text: Bro, there's this app. Put in ₹500 today and you get ₹1,000 back next week. Guaranteed! My cousin already got paid.

choices.consequence: You sent ₹500 to an app you'd never heard of.
Asking how the money is made is the right first step.

choices.text: Say no and tell a parent or teacher
choices.consequence: You kept your money and got a second opinion.

nodes.speaker: Rohan
nodes.text: Don't worry about how. You just have to get two friends to join, and then you get paid from what they put in.

choices.text: Join anyway, Rohan's cousin got paid
choices.consequence: Early joiners get paid with newer joiners' money, until new people stop coming.

choices.text: "So new people's money pays old people? That's a scam."
choices.consequence: You spotted it: no real business, just new money paying old investors.

nodes.text: A week later the app has vanished from the store. Rohan's messages to the "support" number bounce. The ₹500 is gone.

choices.consequence: Reporting fast gives the best chance of stopping it, and protects others.
Staying quiet lets the scam keep finding new people.

nodes.text: Your teacher explains: nobody can guarantee to double money in a week. Real savings and investments grow slowly, and even they aren't guaranteed. You kept your ₹500.
You call the cybercrime helpline 1930 and file a report at cybercrime.gov.in, and you warn your friends. If money was sent through a bank or UPI, tell the bank straight away too.
The app shows up again under a new name, and two classmates lose money too. Being scammed is nothing to be ashamed of. Reporting it is how scams get stopped. Try again?
